messages.subject: Calibration of .bin files
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent,

I understand that GGIR will run a auto-calibration algorithm to come up with a calibration error, and the offset is stored in C object of the basic meta RData file. For some of our population level analysis we will need to convert the .bin files into 60s epochs and analyze the data outside of the GGIR package.

1. How do I use the calibration information to write a new .bin file with the corrected values, and is this necessary?

2. Also in the newest GENEActiv software, I saw that there is an option for setting z-axis temperature offset when converting to 60s epochs. Does this mean that the software automatically applies the activity based auto-calibration when doing the converting?

Best,
Mike

messages.subject: First and last 24h not analysed
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent hi all,

Here's a problem that I hadn't encountered until now:

I use 14 days recordings with a start set at 00:00. (When looking at .csv recording actually start at  ~00:00 (i.e. 00:01:00:500) (because of the potential small difference between device time and local pc time I guess)

Then I use the following for part.1/part.2:

dayborder=0,
strategy=1,
hrs.del.start=0,
hrs.del.end=0,
maxdur=14,
includedaycrit=15,
qwindow=c(0,24),
[...]
do.report=c(2)

For all my files, first and last days are NA in daysummary.

Calendar_date is 00:15:00  for day 1 and day 14 and 00:14:55 for all other days.

For measurement day 1 and 14, N.valid.hours is 0.24 (i.e. 14.4 min) explaining why data are not computed for these days.

Any idea what may cause this issue and what would solve it?

R 3.3.3
GGIR 1.4

Thanks,

Damien

messages.subject: Re: Calibration of .bin files
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mike,

As its name indicates it, the autocalibration performed within GGIR is a procedure that measure and correct potential calibration errors.
If calibration error has not been reduced to under 0.01 g., then data are not processed.
Therefore you can use epoch reduced data .csv  as is.
Information regarding autocalibration for processed data may be find is `data_quality_report.csv`

Refer to the original Vincent's paper regarding autocalibration.  <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4187052/>

Best regards,

Damien

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jairo, Can you change maxdur to 8 and try again? In your current definition all analyses are clipped to zero days of measurement which triggers the error. Maxdur acts like a maximum measurement duration, all data beyond this point will be ignored, so never use maxdur = 0.
Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] First and last 24h not analysed
messages.body_plain:
Hi Damien,
Here are my thoughts:
- Is variable N hours substantially different from N.valid.hours?
- You may want to change argument maxdur to 14.5, such that the analyses also include a bit more than 14 days of data.
- Next, can you have a look at the milestone data (RData) from one of your problematic files and inspect the dimensions of the M$metashort dataframe via command: dim(M$metashort). Do these dimensions matches the 14 days of data you expect?
- Can you also plot the values of the M$metashort$ENMO object to see how the movement pattern varies acros days of measurement?
Best wishes
Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Calibration of .bin files
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mike,

The calibration correction is applied within the GGIR analyses and all output GGIR creates is based on the corrected raw data.
If you want to use any software that is not GGIR to convert raw data to 60 second epochs then I cannot guarantee that calibration correction is used. You would have to contact the developers/maintainer of that software.
I hope this answers your question.

Damien - thanks for your help. Note that if the error is not reduced to under 0.01 the data is still processed but the reported calibration error reduction in the output (e.g. output part2 or object C) should then alarm you as a user to not trust the corresponding results.
Best, Vincent

Here are my thoughts:

- Is variable N hours substantially different from N.valid.hours?

Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Please find a below a summary of a correspondence I had with Pedro Ped...@chuv.ch and Mike yao....@nih.gov regarding an issue they encountered and the solution to address this issue:

Original message by them: "We are trying to analyze the *.bin data from Geneactiv and we obtain the following error when importing the file

[1] "File name: 5754__031468_2017-02-22 11-58-39.bin"

Error in array(x, c(length(x), 1L), if (!is.null(names(x))) list(names(x),  :

  'data' must be of a vector type, was 'NULL'

The bin file was obtained directly from the Geneactiv device and is 715 Mb (15 days). We tried reading it using g.meta but it does not work. Do we also need to upload GENEAread?

I attach the code. Do you have any idea why it is not working? We are running it on a Windows 7 professional environment, 24Gb RAM, and we run the code using Rstudio Version 0.99.879 and R version 3.2.3."

Final solution:

Reinstall the R packages on which GGIR depends, because they are probably out of date. For example, mmap, bitops, matlab...

Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Units of measurement for data under MVPA_E5S_T100_ENMO
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Units of measurement for data under MVPA_E5S_T100_ENMO
messages.body_plain:
Your interpretation is correct. The improvement of the documentation for the variables that are produced by g.part5 (mode = 5) is on my to do list.

For the moment, please find some clarifications on the abbreviations I used in the variable names:

dur = duration, acc = average acceleration, Nblock = number of blocks
D10 = bout lengths with 10 minutes and longer
T120 = threshold of 120 mg and higher
_pla = plain average across available days
_wei = weighted average across available days where weekend days always weighted 2/5 relative to the contribution of week days

If there is no D like in LIG50_120 then it refers to unbouted time spent between those thresholds
dur_LIGB_D10T50_120 are the time spent in bouts of light activity of at least 10 minutes

WW in filename refers to analyses based on the timewindow from waking to waking up, while MM in filename refers to analyses done on windows between midnight and midnight

SIB=sustained inactivity bouts, are the periods of time during which the arm does not rotate at all for at least 5 or 10 minutes (I do not know what criteria you used). This could be daytime sleep or the monitor not being worn for a very short period of time.

INB are bouts of time during which acceleration is below an acceleration threshold for at least X% of the time.

If you have two bout duration thresholds like 1 and 10 minutes you will get D1T100 and D10T100. In this case D1T100 effectively means bouts between 1 and 9.99 minutes, while D10T100 refers to bouts of at least 10 minutes.

TMOD and TVIG are total moderate and total vigorous PA with all bouted and unbouted time contributing. Just MOD and VIG are only the unbouted time spent in those categories.

nightwak = night waking time

SIB= sustained inactivity bouts, can be part of inactivity bouts (INB variables), SIB are the sustained inactivity bouts that are not part of the inactivity bouts. This is why I have a TSIB and a SIB variable, explanation of these are:
TSIB = total of all sustained inactivity bouts (regardless of whether they contributed or not to inactivity bouts (INB).
TOIN = Total other inactivity
TIN = Total inactivity = TOIN + SIB = Total other inactivty + Sustained inactivity

So, basically there are the following levels from least active to most active:
- Sleep or SIB
- Other inactivity
- Light
- Moderate
- Vigorous
Additionally they a grouped in:
- MVPA bouts (Moderate or Vigorous)
- Light bouts (just light)
- Inactivity bouts (Other inactivity or SIB)
- And the non-bouted time spent in each of the five categories
And also as the total of each category: TSIB, TOIN, TLIG, TMOD, TVIG
dur_day_min_pla, dur_night_min_pla, and dur_nightandday_min_pla: duration of a day and night time
The bout criteria for inactivity is 0.9, why is this different to the criteria for light and MVPA which is 0.8? Ssomewhat arbitrary decision, but the idea was that if you allow for bouts of 30 minutes it would not make sense if you allow for breaks of 20% of the time(6 minutes !) this is why I used a more stringent criteria for the highest category
